newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan racketeer in Nomura scandal arrested - TV.
newsitem.headline: Japan racketeer in Nomura scandal arrested - TV.

text.p: Japanese prosecutors probing a payoffs scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd, the country's top brokerage, on Thursday arrested a racketeer at the centre of the affair, Japanese television reported.

Prosecutors arrested Ryuichi Koike, a racketeer who is accused of taking millions of yen in illegal payoffs from Nomura, NHK and TBS television reported. The reports said his brother, a realtor, had also been arrested on suspicion of acting as an accomplice.
On Wednesday, prosecutors arrested three former Nomura executives over a 50 million yen ($431,000) payment to Koike.
"Sokaiya" racketeers extort money from firms by threatening to disrupt shareholders' meetings. Payments to them by firms are forbidden under Japan's commercial code.
The scandal has cost Nomura Securities dearly. Many major clients, including government-backed investment bodies, have stopped doing business with the brokerage as a result.

Earlier in the day, prosecutors raided Nomura's head offices for the second time since the scandal broke in March. Nomura itself also faces possible legal action after Japan's securities watchdog earlier this week asked prosecutors to investigate the firm's role in the scandal. ($1=116 yen)
